take_homes: you can't share an agent. you share context, a skill, output or an interface, and each one needs a different person on the receiving end.
access and absorption are different things. a licence or a bot nobody uses tells you nothing. if there's no named owner, it doesn't get used.
pick what to share by what the teammate's job needs, and write the people plan next to the tech plan. i usually only do the tech.

monday.move: talk to the sales lead about how they prepare for a customer call today, before building anything more. then see whether the weekend sales setup is worth finishing.
monday.when: monday morning, in a 20 minute chat
monday.stop_condition: if she says she has no pain there or doesn't want it, i drop the setup. if she wants it, i name who maintains it before i build further.
monday.blocker: i'll want to build it first and talk to her afterwards. the weekend build is already half done.

misconception.why: the module never made me check an output. the closest was the people-plan line about a polished tech file with unnamed roles, and that is about ownership, not about verifying the agent's work. i still think the spot-check steps are ceremony. what did shift a bit is that 'the agent is good' doesn't mean anyone will use it.

one_line: good for the rollout side, 'you can't copy accountability' is the line i'll remember. a lot of it is prompts i'd skip, and i never saw how to tell the agent's output is right.
